title: Breast Cancer Treatment & Survival
description: Retrospective assessment of standard care in Bangladesh using progression-free and overall survival. The published Kaplan–Meier curves compare five diagnosis groups; the source reports a more favorable prognosis for Luminal A and poorer outcomes for TNBC and HER2-positive disease.
caption: Original IOJH figure · survival probability by diagnosis
alt: Published Kaplan–Meier curves with survival probability from 0 to 1 and time in days for five breast cancer diagnosis groups.

title: Congenital Heart Disease in NICU Neonates
description: Among 61 neonates with congenital heart disease, ASD accounted for 36.1%, VSD for 24.6% and PDA for 19.7%. This case distribution highlights the role of echocardiographic assessment in characterizing the burden of congenital defects in NICU care.
chart: Comparative bar plot for PDA data
sub: Eight patient groups · values shown in the source graph
caption: IOJH comparative bar plot for PDA data
alt: Grouped bar chart comparing Size of PDA, PDA at 5 Days, and PDA Reduction Amount across eight patient groups.

title: Pharmaco-Invasive Strategy & Delayed Primary PCI
description: In Group I (n=59) and Group II (n=45), post-procedure TIMI III flow was reported in 76.27% versus 48.89% (p=0.02). Bleeding occurred in 10.16% versus 28.89% (p=0.04). These observed differences describe reperfusion and safety outcomes; baseline differences limit causal interpretation.
chart: Cox proportional hazards model for pPCI timing
sub: Hazard ratios and 95% confidence intervals · timely, delayed, and late pPCI
caption: Cox proportional hazards model for pPCI timing
alt: Forest plot showing hazard ratios with 95% confidence intervals for timely, delayed, and late pPCI.

title: Clinical Profile & Patterns of Headache
description: An observational study of 100 patients at Dhaka Medical College Hospital (July–December 2013) characterized headache presentation. Compressive pain was reported by 61%, nausea by 60%, vertigo by 34% and photophobia by 33%. These overlapping features describe the clinical profile rather than mutually exclusive diagnoses.
chart: Distribution of study patients by headache character
sub: Number of patients by headache character · 100-patient study
note: Counts may overlap because a patient could report more than one headache character.
caption: IOJH distribution of study patients by headache character
alt: Horizontal bar chart of headache character among study patients. Compressive is most frequent, followed by pulsatile, heavy, dull, penetrating, tingling, burning, and electric shock.

title: Semaglutide Use & Reported Patient Outcomes
description: The 31-patient study reports weight loss in 83.9%, side effects in 64.5% and cost as a challenge in 67.7%. The findings describe reported patient experience and treatment burden; the summary does not provide paired HbA1c measurements or a control group to quantify glycaemic efficacy.
note: Reported outcomes; categories overlap. No HbA1c change inferred.
